title: Equally certain: men use their freedom, and are rightly praised or blamed, rewarded or punished
source_text: XLVI. Nec minus ratione & experientia certum, & etiam scripturae authoritate confirmatum, homines seu bene, sive male agant, libertate sua uti, & ita libere moveri, ut laude vel vituperio, vel poena vel praemio merito digni habeantur, prout bene vel male egerint.
pass_a_gloss: XLVI. Nor is it less certain by reason and experience, and also confirmed by the authority of scripture, that men whether they act well, or ill, use their freedom, and are so freely moved, that they are deservedly held worthy of praise or blame, or punishment or reward, according as they have acted well or ill.
pass_b_english: It is no less certain by reason and experience, and confirmed also by the authority of Scripture, that men use their freedom whether they act well or badly. They are moved so freely that they are rightly held to deserve praise or blame, punishment or reward, according as they have acted well or badly.

lemmas.latin: vel poena vel praemio merito digni habeantur
lemmas.gloss: are deservedly held worthy of punishment or reward

choices.why: The will's freedom; 'freedom' throughout, with 'free choice' for liberum arbitrium.
